result.title: Wire the governed-intake post-merge readback (code#8057) into the native lander for release-touching .github merges (code#8013/#8036 follow-up)
result.body:

## Work type
Task

## Context

code#8057 adds `pnpm github-mcp-worker-intake:readback --producer-commit <sha>`. It produces a post-merge `GovernedIntakeWorkerReadbackV1` receipt showing which governed-intake release the deployed github-mcp-worker resolves and stages. Nothing calls it automatically yet. Historically, code#8045 added a pre-merge consumer-pin check; the accepted code#8197 ruling subsequently retired that direction. Post-merge observation must not restore it. Nothing yet reads the worker back *after* that merge, so an intake outage caused by a release merge is only noticed if someone checks health by hand. That is how code#8013 was noticed.

Non-blocking follow-up from the PR Review of code#8057 @ bab963b97b2c44d988731a1d4f024f856419b115 and code#8045 @ d7bd62b096b170fafdb06c841dc13601bcad6bd5. Refs #8013, #8036.

## Durable fix and acceptance

1. **Automatic, post-merge.** After the native lander (`skills/governed-git-delivery`) merges a `spencer-shadley/.github` PR that touches the governed-intake release, it runs the intake readback with `--producer-commit <the merge commit on .github main>`. No human or agent has to remember to run it. The same holds for `fleet-cli gh pr-merge` on release-touching `.github` PRs, or a tracked issue covers that path.
2. **Bounded retry.** The readback retries for a bounded window that covers a normal worker deploy or cache refresh, with the attempts and interval stated. The final verdict uses the current readback contract (`serving`, `lagging`, `unavailable`, or an indeterminate failed read).
3. **Receipt bound to the land.** The land receipt (`LandResult`) carries the readback receipt: deployed commit, resolved and bundled release identity, expected identity, and verdict. The receipt names the exact `.github` merge commit it judged.
4. **Loud on failure.** Any verdict other than `serving` (including exit 2) after the window is surfaced as a land-receipt failure and opens or updates one deduped owner issue (intake outage after release merge), naming the `.github` merge commit and the worker health readback. It is not reported as a successful land.
5. **Non-release PRs untouched.** `.github` PRs classified `not-release-touching` and all other repositories perform no readback and no extra health GETs.
6. **Quota-aware.** Health GETs are paced (no tighter than one per ~2 minutes by default), because each worker request spends the shared GitHub allowance.
7. **Tests.** Unit tests cover: a release-touching land runs the readback with the merge commit; `serving` is recorded; `lagging` / `unavailable` / exit 2 fail the receipt and route to the owner issue; non-release lands do no readback.

## Triage notes (advisory, triage pulse hourly-1755)
- Historical note, superseded by the current correction below: at Code tip `8d0641e6`, PR #8057 was open and the readback script had not landed. PR #8057 is now merged; do not retain that old dependency or restore #8045's retired consumer-pin check.
- The `fleet-cli gh pr-merge` half of item 1 lives in cli-wrappers; item 1 already allows a tracked issue to cover it.
- Substrate: `cloud-ready`. Lander wiring and receipts are unit-testable with a fake readback in a fresh checkout; a live readback after a real `.github` release merge is a separate verification follow-up.

No human decision required.

## Current dependency and direction correction (2026-10-14)

PR #8057 is CLOSED and merged as `5dbdc83fbc1b06ddf0f9e1b847fc40b420b0bfae`. The current Code tree `3c1abf4beb6ad90b1f263f07c72dfeacde10fdc2` contains `tools/reconcile/github-mcp-worker/intake-release-readback.ts`; the earlier claim that implementation waits for the command to land is superseded.

The accepted ruling https://github.com/spencer-shadley/code/issues/8197#issuecomment-6051567438 removes consumer-pin checks. The bounded settlement https://github.com/spencer-shadley/code/issues/7658#issuecomment-6169153046 explicitly retains #8070's post-merge observability value. #7658 owns pin/copy removal and #8036 owns consumer-pin wiring removal; this issue must not restore either mechanism. Recording the release identity actually observed is evidence, not a pin.

At the inspected tree the readback contract carries `resolved` and `bundled`, and its verdicts are `recorded`, `serving`, `lagging` and `unavailable`; a failed read exits 2 as indeterminate. Historical `prepared` / `staged-not-serving` descriptions are not a current API claim. Automatic observation, paced bounded retries, land-bound receipts and deduplicated outage routing remain acceptance. Preserve the distinction between a merge that occurred and a post-merge observation that failed. No runtime readback, health probe or test was executed here; automatic wiring and live acceptance are not proved by command presence.

This is a bounded source/discussion correction, not canonical triage completion. Existing checklist, labels and completion artifacts are preserved as historical state; no current evaluator, authenticated completion record, new stamp or model provenance is asserted. Current producer delta/semantic completion and any unresolved graph, direction, source-verification or owner handoff remain with their existing owners.
